name: Long tones
description: Low to mid range, eight counts a note against a drone. Tune by ear first, then check the tuner.

name: Dynamic long tones
description: One note, pp to ff and back over sixteen counts. The pitch must not bend on the way.

name: Overtone series
description: Finger low Bb and voice up the overtone series, then match each overtone against its real fingering.

name: Subtone low register
description: Low D down to low Bb, as soft and warm as it goes without cracking.

name: Altissimo entries
description: Attack altissimo notes cold from silence, softly. Stop the moment the sound stops being reliable.

name: Harmonics
description: Finger your lowest note (low D on piccolo) and blow up the harmonic series. Keep the air speed even as the partials climb.

name: Register break crossings
description: Slur across the break both directions, throat A to B with the right hand down, then chromatically either side of it.

name: Lip slurs
description: Low partial to the next and back (trumpet C-G-C, trombone Bb-F-Bb) on each valve combination or slide position, slurred, no tongue.

name: Vibrato pulses
description: Even vibrato pulses against the click: two per beat, then three, then four. Then play a phrase and let it go natural.

name: Mouthpiece pitch bends
description: Mouthpiece alone, or mouthpiece and neck on sax. Hold your reference pitch, then bend down a half step and back with the voicing, not the jaw.

name: Range builder
description: Slurred chromatic steps up from the middle register at 60, setting held and breathing through the nose. Stop at the first thin note and rest as long as you played.

name: Breathing cycles
description: In four out four, in two out six, in one out eight. No instrument, just air.

name: Air attacks
description: Start notes on air alone, no tongue, at pp. Teaches the air to lead the note.

name: Long phrase builder
description: One breath, chromatic scale as far as it reaches at 60. Add a note to the phrase each day.

name: Articulation grid
description: One pitch, eighths at 100. Cycle all tongued, all slurred, two-slur-two, two-tongue-two.

name: Doodle tongue
description: Doo-dle-doo-dle on one pitch, then up a scale. Straight eighths first, then swung.

name: Staccato scales
description: Major scale short and detached, with no gap in the air between notes. Start at 80.

name: Double tonguing
description: Ta-ka in sixteenths on one mid-register pitch, slowly, until the K is indistinguishable from the T.

name: Ghost notes and upbeats
description: Swing eighths up and down a scale: tongue and accent each upbeat, ghost the note before it. Then put it into a bebop line.

name: Chromatic scale, full range
description: Bottom to top and back, four articulations, start at 80 and add 4bpm per clean pass.

name: Finger independence
description: Trill each pair of adjacent fingers eight times through the whole range. Slow, even, relaxed.

name: Scales in fourths
description: Major scale in ascending fourths, one octave then two. Start at 60.

name: Speed bursts
description: A four-note fragment at a tempo you cannot sustain, four repeats, then rest. Accuracy over speed.

name: Major scales around the circle
description: Two octaves where the range allows, eighths at 100, all the way round the circle of fourths.

name: Modes of the major scale
description: One key, all seven modes off each degree, up and down without stopping.

name: Bebop scale
description: Dominant scale with the added natural seven, descending from the root on beat one, so the chord tones land on the beat.

name: Diminished and whole tone
description: Both symmetrical scales from each starting note, eighths, listening for where they repeat.

name: Digital patterns
description: 1-2-3-5 off every degree, then 1-3-5-8 and 3-2-1-7, around the circle.

name: Blues scales around the circle
description: Minor blues scale in every key round the circle of fourths, then the major blues scale. Two octaves where the range allows.

name: Pentatonics around the circle
description: Major and minor pentatonic in every key round the circle, straight up and down, then in four-note groups.

name: Seventh-chord arpeggios
description: Maj7, 7, m7, m7b5 and dim7 from each root round the circle, up to the ninth and back.

name: Subdivision ladder
description: One pitch: quarters, eighths, triplets, sixteenths against a click at 70. Switch on the bar line.

name: Displaced click
description: Metronome on two and four only, scale in eighths. Then click on beat one of alternate bars.

name: Swing eighths at two tempos
description: Eighths over a click at 120, then at 180. Notice exactly where the feel has to change.

name: Sight-read an etude
description: Something you have never played, once through without stopping. Then fix the worst two bars.

name: Etude at half tempo
description: One line at half the marked tempo, played perfectly, then step the tempo up ten percent.

name: Lick around the circle
description: Take one lick and move it through the circle of fourths until it stops needing thought.

name: Lick displacement
description: One lick started on beat one, then two, three, four, then on the upbeats.

name: Enclosures
description: Approach each chord tone from a scale step above and a half step below, then the reverse, through a ii-V-I in every key.

name: ii-V-I guide tones
description: Only the thirds and sevenths through ii-V-I, voice-led, around the circle.

name: ii-V-I arpeggios
description: Arpeggiate each chord up and down, then connect them by the nearest step instead.

name: Minor ii-V-i
description: Half-diminished to altered dominant to minor tonic, around the circle.

name: Rhythm changes A section
description: Just the A section changes: arpeggios first, then a line, slowly enough to hear every move.

name: Basic blues in every key
description: Three-chord 12-bar blues, I7 IV7 V7. Arpeggios through the form, then guide tones, round the circle of fourths.

name: Jazz blues changes
description: Bebop blues: IV7 in bar 2, #IV dim in bar 6, VI7 in bar 8, ii-V in 9 and 10, I-VI-ii-V turnaround. Guide tones in F and Bb, then other keys.

name: Bird blues changes
description: Blues For Alice changes: descending ii-Vs from the I in bar 1 down to the IV in bar 5, more in bars 6 to 8, then the ii-V turnaround. Guide tones first, then arpeggios.

name: Minor blues changes
description: 12-bar minor blues: i, iv, i, then bVI7 to V7alt in bars 9 and 10. Arpeggios, then guide tones, round the circle.

name: Sixteen-bar blues
description: Watermelon Man or Work Song form: the 12-bar shape with extra bars before the turnaround. Solo over the roots and keep your place without counting aloud.

name: Melody from memory
description: Play the head with no chart in front of you. Wherever you stumble is what you do not actually know.

name: Changes without the melody
description: Arpeggiate the changes in time with no melody, so the harmony is the thing you know.

name: Play along with the recording
description: Play the head with a classic recording, matching its phrasing, articulation and where it sits on the beat.

name: One-idea solo
description: Improvise a chorus on exactly one rhythmic idea. The constraint is what makes the ear work.

name: Guide-tone solo
description: Solo using only thirds and sevenths. Nothing else is allowed in.

name: Transcribe four bars
description: Four bars of a solo by ear, no chart. Sing it accurately before you play it.

name: Head by ear
description: Learn the melody from a recording, no chart, a phrase at a time. Sing each phrase before you look for it on the horn.

name: Sing then play intervals
description: Sing an interval, then play it and check yourself. Work outward from a second.

name: Find the interval by ear
description: Drone a note, sing a target interval above it, then find it on the horn without hunting.

name: Chord qualities by ear
description: Have an app or a pianist play seventh chords. Name the quality before checking, then sing the root and the third.

name: Changes by ear
description: Listen to a recording and write the bass roots of the first eight bars before you look at a chart.

name: Rhythm reading
description: Read rhythms on a single pitch, the hardest thing you can find, against a click.

name: Transposition at sight
description: Read a part written for a different transposition than your horn, such as concert to Bb or Eb, or the reverse. Slowly.
